name: Tom Aspinall
bio: Tom Aspinall is the UFC Heavyweight Champion and pound-for-pound one of the best fighters on the planet. A rare combination of elite grappling, explosive striking and genuine heavyweight power, Aspinall has finished every title fight opponent in the first round. The Manchester native captures the interim belt with a 27-second TKO of Pavlovich and became undisputed champion in 2025.

name: Curtis Blaydes
bio: Curtis Blaydes is one of the UFC's most durable heavyweights, a Division I wrestler who uses suffocating top pressure and relentless ground-and-pound to grind down opponents. He has beaten multiple ranked heavyweights and has faced the very best the division has to offer, though recent losses to Aspinall and Hokit have kept the title just out of reach.

name: Sergei Pavlovich
bio: Sergei Pavlovich is one of the most feared knockout artists in heavyweight history, with nine first-round finishes in a row before his title shot at UFC 295. His straight right hand is one of the most dangerous weapons in the division and he owns the fastest KO in heavyweight history. Back on form with consecutive wins in 2025.

name: Ciryl Gane
bio: Ciryl Gane is the most technically gifted heavyweight in MMA, combining elite kickboxing footwork with extraordinary movement that belies his 250-pound frame. A former interim champion, Bon Gamin's only UFC losses are to Ngannou and Pavlovich. His UFC 321 fight with Aspinall was ruled a No Contest after an accidental eye poke, with the rematch now a must-see.

name: Jailton Almeida
bio: Jailton Almeida is a submission grappling specialist whose BJJ black belt technique and relentless top control made him one of the most feared heavyweights in the world. With a 90% finish rate and 17 submissions, his rapid rise through the UFC ranks was electrifying. Released by the UFC after consecutive losses to Volkov and Kuniev in 2025-2026.

name: Alex Pereira
bio: Alex Pereira is one of the most exciting champions in combat sports history, a two-division UFC champion and former Glory Kickboxing world champion whose generational power has produced five first-round knockouts in his last nine UFC fights. He lost the LHW title to Ankalaev at UFC 313 only to immediately reclaim it with a TKO in round one at UFC 320, cementing his status as the face of the sport.

name: Magomed Ankalaev
bio: Magomed Ankalaev is one of the most technically precise fighters in the UFC, a Dagestani with world-class wrestling and sharp technical striking who became LHW champion by defeating Alex Pereira at UFC 313. Although Pereira reclaimed the belt via TKO at UFC 320, Ankalaev proved he belongs at the very top and is the division's most credible long-term threat.

name: Jiří Procházka
bio: Jiří Procházka is the most unconventional fighter in the UFC, combining samurai philosophy with unorthodox wild striking that has produced some of the most memorable finishes in LHW history. A former champion who submitted Glover Teixeira to win the title, Procházka fights without fear and never backs down from a challenge.

name: Khalil Rountree Jr.
bio: Khalil Rountree Jr. is one of the UFC's most improved fighters, transforming from an inconsistent prospect into a legitimate title challenger through relentless work ethic and a six-fight knockout streak. His creative, powerful striking style makes him dangerous against anyone in the division. He challenged Pereira for the LHW title at UFC 307 in a war before falling in round 4.

name: Dricus du Plessis
bio: Dricus du Plessis made history as the first South African UFC champion, stopping all-time greats Strickland, Whittaker, and Adesanya on his way to and in defence of the belt. His relentless forward pressure and ability to take punishment while remaining dangerous is elite. He lost the belt to Chimaev at UFC 319 and is building back toward another title run.

name: Robert Whittaker
bio: Robert Whittaker is a former UFC Middleweight Champion and one of the most technically gifted strikers in the division's history. Crisp combinations, elite footwork and an iron chin have allowed him to beat nearly every top contender. His rivalry with Adesanya defined an era of middleweight MMA and he remains one of the most dangerous fighters at 185.

name: Khamzat Chimaev
bio: Khamzat Chimaev is the UFC Middleweight Champion and one of the most dominant undefeated fighters in MMA history. His elite wrestling, smothering grappling and explosive striking have dismantled everyone placed in front of him. He submitted Whittaker in round one at UFC 308 and then defeated du Plessis by unanimous decision at UFC 319 to claim the belt he was always destined to hold.

name: Sean Strickland
bio: Sean Strickland pulled off one of the biggest upsets in UFC history when he dominated Adesanya for the middleweight belt. His boxing-first style prioritises volume and relentless pressure over power, and his ability to ignore damage while landing clean combinations makes him uniquely difficult to fight. A two-time title challenger who always shows up.

name: Israel Adesanya
bio: Israel Adesanya is a generational striking talent and three-time UFC Middleweight Champion whose anime-influenced style and culture-shifting presence made him one of the most iconic figures in combat sports. A kickboxing world champion turned MMA superstar, Izzy's footwork, timing and counter-striking are among the most technically sophisticated seen in any weight class.

name: Belal Muhammad
bio: Belal Muhammad is a former UFC Welterweight Champion who captured the belt from Leon Edwards with an unstoppable performance at UFC 304. A relentless wrestler and pressure fighter known for suffocating top control, Muhammad has wins over multiple top-five welterweights. He lost the title to Jack Della Maddalena at UFC 315 in a hard-fought decision.

name: Jack Della Maddalena
bio: Jack Della Maddalena is one of the most exciting welterweights in the world, a precision boxer with great timing, elite footwork and devastating finishing power who won the UFC welterweight title at UFC 315 by defeating Belal Muhammad. His clean boxing — crisp jabs, snapping right hands and sharp combinations — is the best in the division. Dropped the belt to Islam Makhachev who moved up in weight.

name: Shavkat Rakhmonov
bio: Shavkat Rakhmonov is one of the last perfectly undefeated elite fighters in the sport, finishing all 18 professional opponents with Sambist grappling and diverse striking. The Kazakh Nomad's blend of creativity and raw power makes him dangerous everywhere. A title shot is inevitable.

name: Leon Edwards
bio: Leon Edwards is a former two-time UFC Welterweight Champion who delivered one of the most iconic moments in MMA history — a walk-off head kick KO in round 5 at UFC 278. Rocky's disciplined boxing and tight gameplan made him champion twice, and he is rebuilding for another run at 170 pounds.

name: Islam Makhachev
bio: Islam Makhachev is the UFC Welterweight Champion and the pound-for-pound number one fighter in the world. A dominant Dagestani wrestler trained by Khabib Nurmagomedov, his top control and submission threat make him nearly impossible to beat. After successfully defending the lightweight title multiple times, he moved up to welterweight and knocked out JDM at UFC 322 to become the 11th double-champion in UFC history.

name: Arman Tsarukyan
bio: Arman Tsarukyan is the most complete lightweight in the world, combining world-class wrestling with powerful boxing, some of the best athleticism in the division, and brutal ground-and-pound from top position. His elbows from top are among the most damaging in the lightweight division. He was scheduled to fight Islam at UFC 311 but pulled out injured — his five-fight win streak, capped with a submission of Dan Hooker, keeps him firmly next in line.

name: Charles Oliveira
bio: Charles Oliveira holds the all-time UFC records for most finishes, most submission victories, and most post-fight bonuses — a relentless BJJ wizard who has become one of the most decorated fighters in the organisation's history. He recently dominated Max Holloway over five rounds to capture the BMF title at UFC 326, adding to a legacy that places him among the all-time greats at 155.

name: Justin Gaethje
bio: Justin Gaethje is the embodiment of action-packed MMA, a relentless pressure fighter whose willingness to trade with anyone has produced some of the most memorable lightweight wars in UFC history. A former interim champion and BMF holder, The Highlight always moves forward. His BMF title run ended in stunning fashion when Holloway KO'd him in round 5 at UFC 300.

name: Ilia Topuria
bio: Ilia Topuria is the UFC Lightweight Champion and the most explosive knockout artist in the sport — undefeated at 17-0 and the first fighter in UFC history to become a two-division champion while remaining unbeaten. El Matador dethroned Volkanovski at FW, stopped Holloway in the rematch, then moved to lightweight and knocked out Oliveira in round one at UFC 317 to add a second belt.

name: Max Holloway
bio: Max Holloway is one of the greatest featherweights in UFC history and a former three-time champion. He won the BMF title at UFC 300 with a stunning last-second KO of Gaethje, then lost it to Charles Oliveira at UFC 326 after a dominant five-round performance from Do Bronx. Blessed's relentless output and elite cardio have made him a fan favourite for a decade.

name: Alexander Volkanovski
bio: Alexander Volkanovski was the longest-reigning UFC Featherweight Champion in history at three years, a former rugby player who built himself into a complete three-time champion through relentless improvement and elite cardio. Despite losses to Topuria and Makhachev, The Great's legacy as arguably the most well-rounded featherweight champion ever is secure.

name: Movsar Evloev
bio: Movsar Evloev is one of the UFC's most underrated unbeaten fighters, a complete martial artist from Ingushetia who uses precise wrestling and technical striking to control fights from start to finish. Unbeaten at 18-0 in professional MMA, his consistency and efficiency make him the featherweight division's most dangerous under-the-radar contender.

name: Jean Silva
bio: Jean Silva is one of the most ferocious strikers in the featherweight division, a Brazilian finisher with a 71% finish rate built on explosive combinations, devastating power and relentless aggression. His striking variety — from sharp punches to spinning attacks — makes him a nightmare stylistically. Won Performance of the Night for a ninja choke finish of Bryce Mitchell and continues to climb toward the title.

name: Merab Dvalishvili
bio: Merab Dvalishvili is a former UFC Bantamweight Champion and the most relentless wrestler in the division, averaging over ten takedown attempts per fight with non-stop cardio that breaks every opponent. He won the belt from O'Malley and made three successful defences before losing a one-sided decision to Petr Yan at UFC 323.

name: Petr Yan
bio: Petr Yan is the UFC Bantamweight Champion and one of the most technically polished strikers in the division's history, with elite boxing precision and relentless pressure that have made him a two-time champion. His demolition of Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 323 — dominating the former champion on the feet and in the clinch — proved he is operating at a different level.

name: Cory Sandhagen
bio: Cory Sandhagen is one of the most creative strikers at bantamweight, a long rangy fighter whose unorthodox attack angles and spinning techniques produce spectacular knockouts. His flying knees and creative striking are matched by a solid wrestling base. He lost a title challenge to Merab at UFC 320 but remains one of the most dangerous fighters at 135.

name: Umar Nurmagomedov
bio: Umar Nurmagomedov is the most dominant young fighter at bantamweight, combining Khabib-style suffocating wrestling with sharper boxing and polished submission game. The Dagestani powerhouse lost for the first time — a close decision to Merab Dvalishvili defending his belt — but remains the division's most exciting prospect for future gold.

name: Alexandre Pantoja
bio: Alexandre Pantoja is the UFC Flyweight Champion and one of the most active BJJ practitioners in the division, constantly threatening submissions from every position. The Cannibal has made multiple title defences, defeating Brandon Moreno twice and Steve Erceg, cementing his status as the best flyweight in the world.

name: Brandon Moreno
bio: Brandon Moreno is a former UFC Flyweight Champion and one of the most beloved fighters in the sport, a high-energy fan favourite from Tijuana who won the title by submitting Deiveson Figueiredo. Moreno and Pantoja's rivalry has defined the flyweight division of the 2020s and his entertaining, aggressive style always delivers for the fans.

name: Valentina Shevchenko
bio: Valentina Shevchenko is one of the greatest female fighters in MMA history, a seven-time UFC Women's Flyweight Champion whose technical mastery, elite striking and championship composure make her the gold standard for women's combat sports. The Bullet has beaten eight former or future champions and remains the greatest flyweight the division has ever produced.

name: Alexa Grasso
bio: Alexa Grasso is a former UFC Women's Flyweight Champion who became a national hero in Mexico when she submitted Valentina Shevchenko at UFC 285. Her slick striking and underrated grappling make her a genuine threat to any champion, and her trilogy with Shevchenko is one of the great rivalries in women's MMA.

name: Zhang Weili
bio: Zhang Weili is a two-time UFC Women's Strawweight Champion and China's biggest MMA superstar, a relentless pressure fighter with elite wrestling, powerful striking and an iron will. Magnum holds the division's longest active title reign and has defeated virtually every elite strawweight of her era.

name: Rose Namajunas
bio: Rose Namajunas is a two-time UFC Women's Strawweight Champion and one of the most technically gifted strikers in women's MMA — a patient counterpuncher with explosive power who has twice knocked out Joanna Jędrzejczyk. Thug Rose's cerebral approach and elite fight IQ give her the ability to dismantle any opponent on a given night.

name: Raquel Pennington
bio: Raquel Pennington is the UFC Women's Bantamweight Champion, achieving gold after over a decade competing at the elite level. Rocky is a durable, well-rounded fighter whose heart and resilience have been on display in the division's toughest fights. Her championship victory was the culmination of years of perseverance.

name: Julianna Peña
bio: Julianna Peña is a former UFC Women's Bantamweight Champion who pulled off one of the greatest upsets in UFC history when she submitted Amanda Nunes. A relentless grappler with elite submission game and cast-iron will, The Venezuelan Vixen brings intensity and aggression that has made her one of the division's most exciting fighters.

name: Jon Jones
bio: Jon Jones is widely regarded as the greatest MMA fighter of all time. A two-time UFC Light Heavyweight Champion and UFC Heavyweight Champion, Bones dominated the LHW division for over a decade with elite wrestling, vicious elbows, creative kicks and the highest MMA IQ ever seen. His only professional loss was a disqualification against Matt Hamill in 2009. He beat Stipe Miocic at UFC 309 in November 2024 to defend the heavyweight title before vacating in 2025.

name: Stipe Miocic
bio: Stipe Miocic is the greatest UFC Heavyweight Champion in history, holding the record for most consecutive heavyweight title defences with four. A firefighter from Ohio who became the most decorated heavyweight the UFC has ever produced, Stipe's clean boxing and wrestling allowed him to defeat Overeem, dos Santos, Cormier (x2) and Ngannou. Retired after a TKO loss to Jon Jones at UFC 309.

name: Anderson Silva
bio: Anderson Silva is the greatest UFC Middleweight Champion of all time and one of the most gifted martial artists the sport has ever seen. His 16-fight UFC win streak and 2,457-day reign as champion remain UFC records. The Spider's combination of Muay Thai precision, clinical front kicks, and almost supernatural ring generalship made him untouchable for nearly a decade. UFC Hall of Fame inductee, 2023.

name: Daniel Cormier
bio: Daniel Cormier is the only active simultaneous two-division champion in UFC history, holding the LHW and HW titles at the same time. A two-time Olympic wrestling alternate who became a combat sports legend, DC's elite grappling and relentless pressure brought him championship gold in two weight classes. All three of his losses came to Jon Jones (twice) and Stipe Miocic.

name: Khabib Nurmagomedov
bio: Khabib Nurmagomedov retired undefeated at 29-0 as the most dominant wrestler in UFC Lightweight history. The Eagle's smothering top control, relentless pressure and ground-and-pound made him impossible to beat — nobody could survive his grappling. He submitted Conor McGregor, Dustin Poirier and Justin Gaethje before retiring in 2020 to honour a promise to his late father.

name: José Aldo
bio: José Aldo is the greatest WEC/UFC Featherweight Champion of all time, holding the 145-pound title for nearly a decade and defending it ten times across two promotions. His devastating leg kicks and ferocious pressure made him one of the most feared strikers in MMA history. A legend of the sport who finally retired following UFC 315 in May 2025.

name: Conor McGregor
bio: Conor McGregor is the biggest star in UFC history and the first fighter to hold two UFC titles simultaneously, capturing the featherweight and lightweight championships in breathtaking fashion. The Notorious's precision left hand, elite timing and unmatched charisma made him a global phenomenon. Currently planning a return to the octagon after nearly five years away.

name: Demetrious Johnson
bio: Demetrious Johnson is the greatest pound-for-pound flyweight in MMA history, holding the UFC record for most consecutive title defences at 11. His combination of elite wrestling, fluid transitions, creative striking and supernatural athleticism made him one of the most complete martial artists the sport has ever produced. Retired in 2024 and will be inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame in 2026.

name: Georges St-Pierre
bio: Georges St-Pierre is the most complete welterweight in MMA history and arguably the greatest UFC champion of all time alongside Jon Jones. Rush held the WW title for nine consecutive defences — a UFC record — and returned from four years away to also capture the Middleweight Championship. His wrestling, boxing, karate and elite conditioning created a game plan-based monster that won fights on every front.

name: Quinton Jackson
bio: Quinton 'Rampage' Jackson is one of the most entertaining and powerful fighters in MMA history, a former UFC and PRIDE Light Heavyweight Champion whose devastating slam KOs and raw knockout power made him one of the sport's most beloved figures. Rampage's charisma, trash talk and warrior mentality made him a superstar in both Japan and America.

name: Randy Couture
bio: Randy Couture is a five-time UFC champion (3x Heavyweight, 2x Light Heavyweight) and one of the founding legends of the sport, proving that technique and heart could overcome physical disadvantages at any age. The Natural won his final championship at 43 years old and was one of the four original inductees into the UFC Hall of Fame. His wrestling-based dirty boxing defined an era.

name: Brock Lesnar
bio: Brock Lesnar is one of the most physically imposing champions in UFC history, an NCAA champion wrestler who became Heavyweight Champion in only his fourth professional fight. His combination of size, power and elite wrestling shocked the world when he knocked out Randy Couture to win the belt. His UFC career was defined by his battles with Cain Velasquez and Junior dos Santos, and he retired after the UFC 200 win over Hunt was overturned.

name: Francis Ngannou
bio: Francis Ngannou is the hardest-hitting MMA fighter in recorded history, the man who dethroned Stipe Miocic with an otherworldly display of power at UFC 260. The Predator's journey from poverty in Cameroon to UFC Heavyweight Champion is one of the most inspiring stories in sports. After leaving the UFC he won the PFL Super Fight HW Championship in 2024 and continues to compete as a free agent.

name: Dustin Poirier
bio: Dustin Poirier is one of the most beloved fighters in UFC history and a two-time interim Lightweight Champion, a blue-collar brawler from Louisiana who improved himself into an elite level fighter. The Diamond holds three wins over Conor McGregor and delivered one of the most iconic moments in the sport when he submitted him at UFC 257. Retired after losing the BMF title fight to Max Holloway at UFC 318 in July 2025.

name: Chuck Liddell
bio: Chuck Liddell is the fighter who put the UFC on the map in mainstream America. The Iceman was the most feared knockout artist in Light Heavyweight history during his peak, with a haymaker right hand that put away icons like Wanderlei Silva, Randy Couture (twice) and Tito Ortiz. His brawling charisma and fearless aggression turned MMA into a mainstream phenomenon in the mid-2000s. UFC Hall of Fame inductee.

name: Chael Sonnen
bio: Chael Sonnen is the greatest trash talker in the history of combat sports — a world-class wrestler who turned every fight week into appointment television with his unmatched verbal warfare. He dominated Anderson Silva for 4.5 rounds in two title fights and repeatedly challenged for the middleweight and light heavyweight belts. His mic work made him a bigger star than most champions ever become.

name: Michael Bisping
bio: Michael Bisping is the first British UFC champion, a relentless pressure fighter who earned his title shot the hard way — fighting 26 times in the UFC before stunning Luke Rockhold with a flash KO at UFC 199. The Count is legendary for his heart and durability, competing with a prosthetic eye and calling out every fighter in the division. A brilliant colour commentator and Hall of Famer.

name: Matt Hughes
bio: Matt Hughes is one of the greatest welterweight champions in UFC history, making six consecutive title defences during his reign and beating icons including BJ Penn, Carlos Newton and Frank Trigg twice. His farm-boy strength and elite wrestling made him the standard-bearer for 170 pounds through most of the 2000s. A two-time champion and UFC Hall of Famer who inspired a generation of fighters.

name: Henry Cejudo
bio: Henry Cejudo is the most decorated combat sports athlete of his generation — an Olympic gold medalist in freestyle wrestling who became a two-division UFC champion at Flyweight and Bantamweight. Triple C defeated Demetrious Johnson (ending his 11-fight title streak), Marlon Moraes, Dominick Cruz and Jose Aldo for his belts before retiring in 2020. His return to face Merab was unsuccessful but his legacy at the top of two divisions remains elite.

name: TJ Dillashaw
bio: TJ Dillashaw is a two-time UFC Bantamweight Champion whose combination of elite footwork, sharp combinations and relentless pressure defined the division for half a decade. His Team Alpha Male defection and rivalry with Cody Garbrandt produced some of the most dramatic moments in bantamweight history. Served a two-year USADA suspension and returned to win the title again before suffering a shoulder injury that ended his run.

name: Dominick Cruz
bio: Dominick Cruz is the most technically sophisticated bantamweight to ever compete, a movement genius whose lateral footwork, level changes and unorthodox angles made him nearly impossible to hit cleanly. A two-time UFC and WEC Bantamweight Champion who overcame repeated severe knee injuries to reclaim championship gold, Cruz remains the blueprint for elite MMA footwork and is now one of the sport's best analysts.

name: Tony Ferguson
bio: Tony Ferguson held the longest winning streak in UFC Lightweight history at 12 fights, an unorthodox brawler with a legendary ground-and-pound, slippery submission game and seemingly superhuman durability. El Cucuy was scheduled to fight Khabib five times — the fight that never happened became MMA mythology. His chaotic style, trash talk and warrior mentality made him one of the most unique figures the sport has produced.

name: Nate Diaz
bio: Nate Diaz is one of the most authentic and beloved fighters in MMA history, a Stockton hardman who never backs down, never changes and never gives an inch. His trilogy with Conor McGregor — including the stunning upset submission at UFC 196 — is among the most iconic in the sport. A BMF title holder, elite submission game and legendary durability make him a cult figure for a generation of fight fans.

name: Donald Cerrone
bio: Donald Cerrone holds the all-time UFC records for most wins (23) and most finishes (16) — a Cowboy who never ducked anyone and fought anyone, anytime, anywhere. His relentless fight schedule, devastating front kick and submission game made him one of the most exciting fighters of his generation. Cerrone always showed up for the fans and was rewarded with more Fight of the Night bonuses than any other fighter in history.

name: Amanda Nunes
bio: Amanda Nunes is the greatest female fighter in MMA history, a two-division UFC champion who demolished every elite woman placed in front of her. The Lioness held the Bantamweight and Featherweight titles simultaneously, obliterating Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg, Valentina Shevchenko (twice), Miesha Tate and Holly Holm along the way. She retired in 2023 as the undisputed GOAT of women's MMA.

name: Joanna Jędrzejczyk
bio: Joanna Jędrzejczyk is one of the greatest female strikers in MMA history, a five-time champion across multiple promotions who dominated the UFC Strawweight division with ferocious Muay Thai striking and elite pressure. Her epic rematch with Zhang Weili at UFC 248 — widely considered the greatest women's fight ever — ended in a split decision loss that left both fighters unrecognisable. Retired in 2022.

name: Cain Velasquez
bio: Cain Velasquez was the most physically dominant heavyweight in UFC history during his peak, a conditioning machine who smothered opponents with relentless top pressure, a suffocating pace and elite wrestling. He twice defeated Junior dos Santos and stopped Brock Lesnar to claim and defend the Heavyweight Championship, but chronic injury problems sadly cut short what should have been a longer reign at the top.

name: Robbie Lawler
bio: Robbie Lawler is one of the most exciting fighters the UFC has ever produced, a pure fighter with iron chin, brawling heart and devastating power who earned his Welterweight Championship the hard way after being cut and returning years later. His wars with Johny Hendricks, Carlos Condit and Rory MacDonald are among the greatest fights in UFC history. Ruthless never backed down.

name: BJ Penn
bio: BJ Penn is one of the most naturally gifted martial artists in UFC history, the first man to win a world championship in two weight classes and a BJJ black belt who received that rank faster than almost anyone in history. The Prodigy's slick submissions, underrated boxing and warrior mentality made him a legend at Lightweight and Welterweight. His rivalry with Frankie Edgar and GSP defined eras in both divisions.

name: Frankie Edgar
bio: Frankie Edgar is one of the most durable and determined fighters in UFC history, a former Lightweight Champion who kept coming back despite being undersized in every division he competed in. His two-fight series with BJ Penn (both wins), elite wrestling and relentless forward pressure defined an era. The Answer never quit, earning the respect of everyone in the sport over a remarkable 16-year UFC career.

name: Vitor Belfort
bio: Vitor Belfort is one of the most naturally gifted strikers in UFC history, The Phenom whose explosive speed and power handed losses to legends like Randy Couture, Dan Henderson and Luke Rockhold. A former UFC Heavyweight Champion and Light Heavyweight title challenger, Belfort also turned to boxing later in career for high-profile bouts. His early career explosiveness was something the sport had never seen.

name: Tito Ortiz
bio: Tito Ortiz was the face of the UFC during its mainstream breakthrough years, a charismatic Bad Boy whose feuds with Chuck Liddell, Randy Couture and Ken Shamrock drew massive PPV numbers and helped establish MMA as a real sport. A three-time LHW champion, Ortiz's grappling-based style and over-the-top persona made him a superstar when the UFC needed stars the most.

name: Wanderlei Silva
bio: Wanderlei Silva is the most terrifying fighter PRIDE ever produced — The Axe Murderer was a walking highlight reel of brutal KO power and relentless aggression who owned the PRIDE Middleweight division for years. His flying knees, savage overhand lefts and complete disregard for his own safety made him the most feared man in Japanese MMA during the golden era. A Hall of Famer and legend of the sport worldwide.

name: Urijah Faber
bio: Urijah Faber is the most influential smaller fighter in MMA history, the California Kid who built Team Alpha Male into a world-class training camp and popularised the bantamweight and featherweight divisions long before they were UFC staples. A former WEC Featherweight Champion with incredible submission game and durability, Faber's multiple championship shots and mentorship of champions like TJ Dillashaw cement his legacy.

name: Carlos Ulberg
bio: Carlos Ulberg is the UFC Light Heavyweight Champion — a decorated kickboxer turned MMA destroyer with an elite 19-2 kickboxing record before transitioning to MMA. The Auckland-born Black Jag brings textbook Muay Thai timing, explosive knockout power, and ice-cold composure. He claimed the vacant LHW title with a first-round KO of Jiří Procházka at UFC 327, putting the entire division on notice. Trained alongside Israel Adesanya at City Kickboxing, Ulberg is the ultimate expression of striker's precision fused with relentless finishing instinct.

name: Carlos Prates
bio: Carlos Prates is the most dangerous finisher in the welterweight division — a Brazilian Muay Thai nightmare who uses every single limb as a weapon. Knees at the clinch, spinning back kicks, vicious elbows, and heavy overhand rights all flow out of the same terrifying combination sequences. Prates fights in a flow state — his offense reads like improvised jazz, unpredictable and relentless. He holds the most knockdowns in UFC Welterweight history and the most KO/TKOs of any fighter in the promotion since 2024. At 6'1" with elite reach, he creates and closes distance at will. His TKO of Jack Della Maddalena at UFC Perth cemented him as a title contender.

name: Mauricio Ruffy
bio: Mauricio Ruffy is the most electric knockout artist in the lightweight division — a Brazilian one-punch destroyer who turns fights off with surgical precision. Named after Monkey D. Luffy from One Piece by his late brother before his first pro fight, Ruffy carries that tribute into every performance. With 12 knockouts in 13 wins, his KO rate is extraordinary for any division. His signature spinning wheel kick has ended multiple fights, earning back-to-back Performance of the Night bonuses on his UFC debut run. At just 27 years old, 'One Shot' Ruffy is already being talked about as a future lightweight champion.

name: Caio Borralho
bio: Caio Borralho is one of the most technically complete middleweights on the roster — a Brazilian prodigy who holds a BJJ black belt, Muay Thai black belt, and Judo brown belt, and actually knows how to use all of them. Borralho is a 'fighting nerd' in the best sense: he studies opponents obsessively and fights with chess-match precision, mixing elite wrestling defense with guillotine traps, pressure striking, and takedowns at exactly the right moment. A relentless competitor who was robbed in his fight against Imavov, Borralho bounced back immediately with a dominant win over Reinier de Ridder. He's quietly building a top-5 résumé that screams future champion.

name: Sean O'Malley
bio: Sean 'Sugar' O'Malley is one of the most entertaining bantamweights in UFC history — an elite striker with flashy footwork, pinpoint accuracy, and a highlight-reel finish rate that makes him a must-watch every fight. He captured the UFC Bantamweight Championship at UFC 292 by stopping Aljamain Sterling, defended it against Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 306, but then lost the rematch via submission at UFC 316. At just 30, he remains a top-5 bantamweight and one of the biggest stars in the sport.
